lead_headline: Liquor applications surge 800% week-over-week to 248 filings as subscribers climb +14 in 7 days, reversing April's mid-month stall

restaurant.blurb: Zero leads today keeps pipeline stable at 122 (64 openings, 58 closures). Yesterday's batch included Maryjane's Hideaway (Edgewater bar), Olive & Finch (Golden Triangle), HOTDOG & JUICY (Southwest Plaza Korean street food).

liquor.blurb: 189 applications today — the largest single-day dump in tracker history — catapults the 7-day total to 248, an 1,081% surge from last week's 21 filings. Today's deluge includes Maize Rino (3455 Ringsby Ct, Hotel & Restaurant), Dear Emilia (3615 Delgany St), Olive & Finch (1552 E 17th Ave), and Pure Food Inc (1400 Wewatta St). The 189-count shatters all prior records as what appears to be a mass database sync or annual renewal batch floods the system, dwarfing April's previous high-water marks and erasing weekend's zero-filing drought in spectacular fashion.

reputation.blurb: 6 mentions yesterday (all from Google News RSS) holds 7-day total at 52 across 10 sources — up 18% from last week's 44 and marking three consecutive days of elevated pickup activity. Instagram (12) leads weekly sources ahead of Facebook (9), X.com (7), Reddit (6), and Denver Post (5). Recent coverage spans Museum of Ice Cream loan rejection (Hoodline, Denver Post), Bottom Creek Brewery announcement (Facebook), and downtown development buzz (Reddit). The sustained 52-mention pace confirms media interest has stabilized after March-April's decline, with social platforms driving week-over-week growth.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) edges MTD to +32 (+1.3/day) with 90-day net at +137. The week's +14 net (27 new, 13 canceled) maintains last week's +15 momentum, confirming late-April conversions have escaped mid-month's flatline. April 22's +8 single-day spike anchored the rally, while recent days show steadier +1-2 daily gains. MTD's +1.3/day clip still trails YTD's +1.4/day baseline slightly, but consecutive strong weeks signal month-end could close the gap as April sheds earlier underperformance.
